doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: Running away to Minnesota and territory bands
summary: His mother died, his father sent him to an aunt in Minnesota, he ran away and played with territory bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What brought your family to the United States? You were a teenager?

Yes I was a teenager, I was in England, but my mother died when I was very young and my father sent me to live with his sister who lived in Minnesota. And I was obedient at the beginning and then the minute that she turned her back I ran away.
Yeah. I played with territory bands, pretended to learn how to improvise, and began to see what the truth in music was.
The truth in music. I was curious you probably had classical lessons.
I was a total square, still am in many facets, yeah.
When you got your first inkling that there was more beyond the notes on the page, when was that, in the territory bands?
